targets.approach: Park at the Glacier Gorge lot (or take the shuttle) and follow the trail toward Black Lake by way of Mills Lake. At Black Lake, skirt the right shore and scramble up beneath the long fracture that leads to the base of Arrowhead, then angle left up grassy ledges into the cirque. The line sits on the left portion of the face, between the upper ramp that leads to the summit and the ledge used for access, immediately left of several dihedrals that run the whole height.
targets.name: Orange Pillar

targets.approach: Park in the pulloff just past the eighteenth highway marker (an interpretive sign about sheep stands there). Walk down the same gullies used for Zeb's Arete, keeping to the left side of the gully; once you are some hundreds of feet lower, the formation appears on your left. It faces east and begins in a splitter that faces right, toward the formation's right flank.
targets.name: Walking Pneumonia

targets.approach: Walk north from the lakeside parking and cross the hill ahead. Beyond the col, look along the top of the cliff for rappel anchors; at this altitude the usual way to reach the wall is to rappel in. Make several rappels down the standard descent, then go around the corner to the base near Cannonball Corner and Undertow; the route itself climbs the arete right of Road Warrior.
targets.name: Black Mamba

targets.approach: Walk north from the lakeside parking and cross the hill ahead. Past the col, look for anchors along the cliff top; the wall is reached most simply by rappelling, though you can also drop from the col and walk beneath the cliffs to the base. The route starts up the opening crack of Good Evans and traverses in from that line toward the roof of Cary Granite.
targets.name: Harry Caray

targets.approach: Choice's Buttress is a south-facing buttress a short way north-east of Freya Tower in the Gore Range. Start in the middle of the south-facing slab and follow the crack system up the centre to a ledge.
targets.name: Door of Light

targets.approach: Choice's Buttress is a south-facing buttress a short way north-east of Freya Tower in the Gore Range. Start in the middle of the south-facing slab, follow the crack system to a ledge, then move right onto the steeper west-facing wall just right of a dihedral and overhang.
targets.descent_text: Walk off around to the west.
targets.name: Timeless Visons

targets.approach: Take County Road 390 past Clear Creek Reservoir through Vicksburg to Forest Road 381, then hike or drive up Forest Road 381 to Clohesy Lake. Walk around the east side of the lake and up to the wall. The route follows the most obvious crack system near the west end of the face.
targets.descent_text: Take the grassy ramp on the west side down to the lake.
targets.name: Way Out

targets.approach: Hike to Shelf Lake. Head north from the lake to a series of stepped cliffs, which lead to a large talus slope and on up to the summit; this is the east ridge of Thatchtop Mountain. The steps in the cliffs are the technical part of the route.
targets.name: East Ridge

targets.approach: Leave the car at George's Corner, above the Glen Cove brake check, and follow the old access road to the abandoned mine; keep the mine on your right and climb talus to the north-facing Fairy Tale Wall, which sits between the Little Pigs and the Chimney. Start on the crack system that trends right through the bottom tier; the route links all four main tiers.
targets.descent_text: Go up and to the left, then follow the ridge that separates the Blue Run and Pigs ski lines back down.
targets.name: Fairy Tale Direct

targets.approach: Approach as for The Anvil and the Rolling Stones Wall, then go down the gully of ferns to the right (skier's right) and follow the foot of the north-facing cliff band to the Fern Gully Spire. The route climbs the north face of the spire by linking crack systems to the airy top.
targets.name: Spooky Scary Skeletons

targets.approach: Park at the roadside pulloff for the crag and hike into the screefield below it; the rock on the approach is very loose. It begins at the Crack Shack's left end, under an enormous right-facing corner holding offwidths, and follows the stark splitter on the north-facing shield above a mid-level terrace.
targets.descent_text: Either rappel to the west from just below the ledge using the tat and ring there, or scramble up the broken ground above and walk down Big Blue.
targets.name: Crack Thief

targets.approach: The Headlands is the highest tier above Wild Tower. It is reached from the top of Wild Tower by heading north: a grassy east-facing gully drops at third class to the right, and the routes lie farther uphill past a large arched roof. This line starts a few feet uphill from Marine Layer, where you step into a right-angling crack.
targets.name: Mosquito Coast

targets.approach: The route is on Old Ironsides Slab. It starts from the top of the big triangular flake in the middle of the slab and goes straight up and over the arch to the first belay of Excitable Boy, on face and friction.
targets.descent_text: Finish up Excitable Boy or Keelhauled, or rappel the line.
targets.name: Der Kinder

targets.approach: The route is on Old Ironsides Slab. It starts at the first belay of Excitable Boy, angles right past the bolt and climbs straight to the anchor shared with that route.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the shared belay anchor, the one used for Excitable Boy.
targets.name: Keelhauled

targets.approach: Drive up Highway 103 on Mount Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans). The slabs are close to the road above Lincoln Lake, shortly before Summit Lake; use one of the small pulloffs on the drop-off side at and just after the corner where the road crosses over the top of the last cliff. The line follows Jabba to the chains on the ledge to its left, below the point where the splitter arcs to the right.
targets.name: Unknown 5.10+

targets.approach: From Telluride drive south toward Lizard Head Pass, then continue south past the pass to a dirt road signed for the Cross Mountain trailhead and park there. Take the trail to a pass between Cross Mountain and Lizard Head, go up the grass shoulder, then follow the climber's trail to the base and around to the right for the south-face routes. This line replaces the third pitch of the standard route, on the southwest side of the summit block, to the right of the standard chimney, starting at a small V-shaped notch above the second-pitch talus.
targets.descent_text: The route ends at the chains where the standard third pitch ends; from there the descent is by rappel with some downclimbing.
targets.name: Mark of Zorro

targets.approach: Begin at Summit Lake, descend to the upper Chicago Lake and contour east along the foot of the cliff to the route you want. A big left-facing cleft divides the main wall above the lakes, and this line runs up the middle of the wall.
targets.name: Kazeemo

targets.approach: It climbs the south-facing Chessboard Wall, high in Oil Creek on Pikes Peak's southwest side. The lower Oil Creek valley is private land, so work out a line through national forest that avoids trespass. One public-land option follows the trail to Horse Thief Park and heads east up the drainage above the falls. Look for the conspicuous arching crack that sweeps left to right.
targets.name: Dreams of Wild Horses

targets.approach: This crag lies in the Abyss Lake basin on the Mount Evans side. It is reached by descending from the road and traversing south, nearly as far as Corner Buttress and the Wind Tower. The line follows broken cracks, one of them an offwidth, on the west-facing left side of a huge, wide-angled open book.
targets.name: Teetering
targets.peak: On the Edge of the Abyss

targets.approach: Park at either entrance to the powerline trail; both lead to the crag, which sits on the right-hand side of the trail a short walk from the second entrance. Small cliffs appear first and grow into notable ones. The route is on the right side of the powerline trail and easy to spot.
targets.name: You Did Good, $lick

targets.approach: This line is on the Pericle, a granite formation not far below the summit of Pikes Peak. The route opens with a wide corner that leads to the foot of a clear hand crack.
targets.name: Arching Jams

targets.approach: The Possibility Area can be reached from the Mount Blue Sky road by hiking to the notch just right of a minor outcrop to the southwest and rappelling into the feature, or from Echo Lake by the Chicago Lakes trail and then left at the fork toward the outcrop in the meadow. This route starts at a bolted belay on the midway ledge of the Possibility Wall, climbs a corner to a rest, and then traverses an undulating rail.
targets.name: A Vacation From Your Problems

targets.approach: The Possibility Area can be reached from the Mount Blue Sky road by hiking to the notch just right of a minor outcrop to the southwest and rappelling into the feature, or from Echo Lake by the Chicago Lakes trail and then left at the fork toward the outcrop in the meadow. Aqualung is on the midway ledge of the Possibility Wall and follows the giant flake.
targets.name: Aqualung

targets.approach: The Possibility Area can be reached from the Mount Blue Sky road by hiking to the notch just right of a minor outcrop to the southwest and rappelling into the feature, or from Echo Lake by the Chicago Lakes trail and then left at the fork toward the outcrop in the meadow. Baby Steps starts at the base of the Possibility Wall, up the obvious weakness at the left side, which can also be used to get up to the midway ledge.
targets.name: Baby Steps

targets.approach: The Possibility Area can be reached from the Mount Blue Sky road by hiking to the notch just right of a minor outcrop to the southwest and rappelling into the feature, or from Echo Lake by the Chicago Lakes trail and then left at the fork toward the outcrop in the meadow. Back to the Earth starts from a bolted belay on the midway ledge of the Possibility Wall, climbs a corner to a rest stance, then continues on steep bolted ground.
targets.name: Back to the Earth

targets.approach: The Possibility Area can be reached from the Mount Blue Sky road by hiking to the notch just right of a minor outcrop to the southwest and rappelling into the feature, or from Echo Lake by the Chicago Lakes trail and then left at the fork toward the outcrop in the meadow. The Corner Route starts at the base of the Possibility Wall and follows the main corner weakness to the top of the wall.
targets.name: Corner Route (Original Aid Route)

targets.approach: The Possibility Area can be reached from the Mount Blue Sky road by hiking to the notch just right of a minor outcrop to the southwest and rappelling into the feature, or from Echo Lake by the Chicago Lakes trail and then left at the fork toward the outcrop in the meadow. It's a Homonym is on the midway ledge of the Possibility Wall and ascends the steep face set within an overhanging gully.
targets.name: It’s a Homonym

targets.approach: The Possibility Area can be reached from the Mount Blue Sky road by hiking to the notch just right of a minor outcrop to the southwest and rappelling into the feature, or from Echo Lake by the Chicago Lakes trail and then left at the fork toward the outcrop in the meadow. Rocky Mountain High is on the midway ledge of the Possibility Wall and takes the big corner.
targets.name: Rocky Mountain High

targets.approach: The Possibility Area can be reached from the Mount Blue Sky road by hiking to the notch just right of a minor outcrop to the southwest and rappelling into the feature, or from Echo Lake by the Chicago Lakes trail and then left at the fork toward the outcrop in the meadow. Tenacious P starts at the base of the Possibility Wall, up a finger crack immediately right of Baby Steps, which can also be used to reach the midway ledge.
targets.name: Tenacious P

targets.approach: From Grand Lake, the North Inlet trail passes Lake Nokoni and ends at Lake Nanita, with the Ptarmigan Towers as its scenic backdrop; counting from the right, they run from one to five. Pika Kombat takes the southeast face of Tower 4, toward its left side. It opens in a small, shallow left-facing dihedral and soon moves right to a distinct crack leading up to a ledge.
targets.descent_text: The line is equipped for rappelling, so the descent is made down the route on its anchors.
targets.name: Pika Kombat (PK)

targets.approach: From Grand Lake, the North Inlet trail passes Lake Nokoni and ends at Lake Nanita, with the Ptarmigan Towers as its scenic backdrop; counting from the right, they run from one to five. Unoriginal Sin climbs the southeast face of Tower 2, starting in a shallow right-facing dihedral just left of the major right-facing dihedral at the centre of the face.
targets.descent_text: Scramble down west from the summit on fourth-class ground, then back north to the trail.
targets.name: Unoriginal Sin

targets.approach: Rescue Rock is a small outcrop just north of US 285 along County Road 60 near Grant. LKP is an easy trad line with a small overhanging roof at the top-out, protected with a standard rack of cams.
targets.descent_text: Walk off to the climber's left (east) by descending a short chimney or crack, or rappel from rocks at the top.
targets.name: LKP

targets.approach: This north-facing buttress in the Gore Range can be reached two ways. The simpler way starts at the Rock Creek trailhead, follows the Freya Tower approach, and then drops southeast into the valley below to the buttress. The other follows the Gore Range Trail south to the bridge over South Rock Creek, then bushwhacks west up the creek past meadows and small outcrops to the base. The route starts at a small rock pillar at the foot of the climb, directly beneath the obvious offwidth on the second pitch.
targets.name: Feel The Rain On Your Skin
